title: Editorial checklist
use_cases: Use when developing a top-level content strategy or editorial roadmap
Implement when selecting media formats to support specific narrative goals
Configure when optimizing article introductions for SEO and user search intent
Use when pruning redundant observations to maintain a coherent takeaway
content:
Decide early on your thesis, structure, and proof points. Then choose the best format for those proof points: text for nuance, audio for intimacy, video for comparison. Write the intro so it immediately answers why this reinterpretation matters now. That “why now” hook is especially important for SEO because it aligns your content with search intent and cultural timing.

Here, it helps to think like a curator. A strong editorial plan resembles concert programming: each section should build tension, release it, and leave the audience with a coherent takeaway. Avoid stuffing the piece with every observation you have. Choose the ones that best explain your reading and support your audience promise.
